Christa Pike Execution Halted Amid Concerns Over Botched Procedure

The execution of Christa Pike, the only woman on Tennessee's death row, was halted shortly before it was scheduled to occur. The 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals issued a temporary stay to consider Pike's claim that her allegations of childhood sexual abuse were not adequately addressed during sentencing. Reports indicate that Pike was in critical condition in a hospital after the execution attempt, with witnesses describing her arm as feeling like it was "about to burst." This event marks the first time Tennessee has prepared to execute a woman in over 200 years, with the last execution of a woman in the state occurring in 1819.
